Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Rivera, Chief Operating Officer; Jordan Lee, VP of Exploration; Lisa Chen, VP of Marketing; and Tom Patel, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production volumes averaging 265,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 6% quarter-over-quarter and 10% year-over-year. I'm particularly pleased with our midstream segment performance, where transportation volumes hit new highs and infrastructure projects ramped up successfully. We are focused on our production guidance for next quarter and the full year, balancing growth catalysts like new well completions with natural declines. Further, we continue to drive down lifting costs per BOE through targeted initiatives. We are advancing key ESG initiatives, making strong progress on emissions reduction targets. Finally, we are taking steps to strengthen our debt position, with net debt declining meaningfully.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. As Dr. Vasquez mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.8 billion, up 15% year-over-year. Operating income was $850 million, and net income was $580 million. We generated $720 million in free cash flow and returned $420 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $5.2 billion in total debt and $1.1 billion in cash.

Let me now turn to our midstream segment, which continues to deliver resilient, fee-based cash flows and underpin our overall portfolio. Midstream represents about 35% of our consolidated EBITDA, driven primarily by our extensive pipeline network, rail terminals, and fractionation facilities. In Q3, the segment generated $450 million in adjusted EBITDA, up 12% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, with margins expanding to 68% from 65% last year. This outperformance reflects strong transportation volumes amid robust upstream activity, coupled with the ramp-up of several key infrastructure projects.

Starting with volumes, we achieved average daily throughput of 2.8 million barrels per day of crude oil equivalents across our system—our highest quarterly figure ever, surpassing our prior record by 8%. This was fueled by a 15% year-over-year increase in Permian Basin volumes, which now account for 65% of our total crude transport, hitting 1.8 million barrels per day. The Permian takeaway capacity deficit has largely resolved since the IPF 2 constraints lifted earlier this year, but we're still capturing significant upside from DUC conversions and new drilling by operators like Pioneer and Occidental.

Breaking it out by commodity: Crude oil totaled 1.6 million barrels per day, up 18% year-over-year. Our Longhorn Pipeline, in JV with DCP Midstream, operated at 95% utilization, transporting 750,000 barrels per day from the Delaware Basin to Nederland, Texas. WTI-Midland spreads tightened to just $0.75 per barrel in Q3—our narrowest in two years—thanks to EPIC Crude's Y-grade integration and new Gulf Coast connectivity. We also saw a 22% year-over-year ramp in Bakken volumes to 350,000 barrels per day via our Dakota Access System stake, benefiting from Hess and Continental's sustained activity despite rail competition from STB-approved unit trains.

Natural gas volumes reached 4.2 billion cubic feet per day, a 10% year-over-year increase. Appalachia dry gas volumes grew 14% to 2.1 billion cubic feet per day on our Mountain Valley Pipeline system, now at full 2.0 billion cubic feet per day capacity following FERC approval of the Southgate extension. This positions us to serve LNG export demand from Cove Point and future Plaquemines LNG cargoes. Permian associated gas hit 1.8 billion cubic feet per day, with our Waha Hub gathering fees averaging $0.28 per MMBtu under take-or-pay contracts covering 85% of capacity.

NGLs came in at 450,000 barrels per day, up 9% year-over-year, driven by fractionation at our Mont Belvieu facility. Propane exports surged 25% amid winter demand in Asia, with Mont Belvieu C3 prices holding a $0.15 per gallon premium to Mont Belvieu over OPIS Gulf Coast indices.

Capacity utilization across our 12,000-mile pipeline network averaged 92%, with firm transportation contracts backstopped at 80% of capacity, insulating us from Waha pricing volatility that dipped to negative $1.50 per MMBtu mid-quarter. Sequentially, volumes were flat to Q2 due to seasonal refinery turnarounds at Motiva and Phillips 66, but we expect a 5-7% quarter-over-quarter rebound in Q4 as Gulf Coast utilization climbs toward 95%.

Regionally, the Permian remains our growth engine, contributing 55% of segment EBITDA, while Appalachia and Bakken each added 15-20% gains from wet gas richness and crude quality premiums. We navigated Hurricane Idalia disruptions with zero downtime, thanks to our automated SCADA systems and dual-redundant power feeds.

Shifting to infrastructure, our $1.2 billion midstream capex program is tracking on plan, with 70% allocated to growth projects yielding IRRs above 15%. We've placed three major assets in service this year, adding 1.2 million barrels per day of takeaway capacity. Key highlights include the Permian Connector Pipeline: Our 550-mile, 36-inch mainline from Waha to Corpus Christi came online in August at 800,000 barrels per day initial capacity, expandable to 1.2 million barrels per day via compressor adds. Backed by 10-year take-or-pay agreements with EQT and Devon at $0.45 per barrel tariffs, it's already at 88% utilization. This de-bottlenecks Delaware Basin producers and captures $20-30 million in annual synergies with our downstream crude trading desk.

NGL fractionation expansion Phase 2 at our Hobbs, New Mexico plant added 30,000 barrels per day of C2/C3 capacity, integrating with ONEOK's Roadrunner system. We're leveraging machine learning algorithms for real-time ethane rejection optimization, reducing flaring by 25% and boosting recovery yields to 98%.

Appalachia gas processing via the $300 million MVP Southgate lateral, a 50/50 JV with Equitrans, secured Virginia DEQ permits and spudded construction in September. This 40-mile, 42-inch line will deliver 1.0 billion cubic feet per day to the Southeast power market by Q4 2025, with tolling fees of $0.25 per Dth and carbon capture tie-ins targeting 90% methane emissions reduction via our partnership with Baker Hughes' Cervus tech.

We're also advancing digital initiatives: Deployed fiber-optic DTS across 40% of our crude lines for predictive leak detection, cutting O&M costs by 12% or $15 million annually. Electrification pilots on Permian pump stations, powered by renewables from NextEra, have slashed Scope 1 emissions by 18% while qualifying for IRA tax credits worth $40 million.

Looking ahead, our 2024 midstream capex guidance remains $1.2-1.3 billion, with $800 million in sanctioned projects including the Gray Oak expansion tie-in and Bakken rail-to-pipe conversions. ROIC on new builds is tracking 18-20%, well above our 12% hurdle. Strategically, midstream remains our cash flow fortress—92% fee-based—with minimal commodity exposure. We're capitalizing on the LNG export boom, where U.S. volumes hit 12 billion cubic feet per day in Q3, and Permian production growth projected at 500,000 barrels per day in 2024 per EIA. Risks like FERC policy shifts are mitigated by our 75% pre-FID contracting. ESG-wise, we're on track for net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2040, with CCUS pilots on our CO2 lines injecting 2 million metric tons per annum by 2026. For Q4, we guide midstream EBITDA to $460-480 million, implying 10-13% full-year growth. This supports our raised 2024 dividend and $2 billion buyback authorization.

I'd now like to dive into our Q3 production results, which were a strong highlight amid the volatile macro environment. We reported average net daily production of 265,000 BOE per day, up 6% quarter-over-quarter from 250,000 BOE per day in Q2 and 10% year-over-year from 240,000 BOE per day in Q3 2023. This performance underscores the early payoffs from our 2024 capital program, particularly in the Permian Basin, where we've leaned into efficiency gains from our optimized frac designs and extended laterals.

Breaking it down by commodity—and we're reporting on a net basis after royalties—oil volumes averaged 162,000 barrels per day, our highest quarterly figure on record. That's an 8% quarter-over-quarter increase from 150,000 barrels per day in Q2 and a robust 16% year-over-year lift from 140,000 barrels per day last year. The quarter-over-quarter uptick was driven by first oil from our 12-well Catarina pad in the Eagle Ford, where initial production rates averaged over 1,800 barrels per day per well, thanks to our cube development strategy and enhanced proppant loading—up 20% from our 2023 designs. In the Permian Delaware, we brought online 18 Midland wells with 30% longer laterals than our 2023 vintage, hitting average 24-hour IPs of 2,200 barrels per day and 7 million cubic feet per day per well. These assets are outperforming our pre-drill type curves by about 15% on EUR, which bodes well for our long-term inventory.

Regionally, the Permian contributed 68% of our total oil volumes, up from 65% in Q2, reflecting the ramp in our D&C activity to 28 rigs from 25. Eagle Ford oil held steady at around 25,000 barrels per day, bolstered by ESP installations on 40% of our new Eagle Ford wells, which have extended run times and boosted recoveries by 10-15%. Offshore Gulf of Mexico volumes were flat quarter-over-quarter at 12,000 barrels per day, as we deferred some subsea tie-backs amid vessel constraints, but we're on track for Q4 upside from our Lobster field Phase 2.

Shifting to natural gas, we averaged 618 million cubic feet per day, or roughly 103,000 BOE per day equivalent using our standard 6:1 conversion. This marks a modest 3% quarter-over-quarter gain from 600 million cubic feet per day in Q2 but was essentially flat year-over-year. The sequential increase came from associated gas off our Permian oil pads—where gas-oil ratios held at 3.5 thousand cubic feet per barrel—and contributions from our Haynesville JV with EQT, where we spudded 15 Utica-shale hybrid wells targeting richer gas windows. However, year-over-year stability reflects deliberate curtailments in the Haynesville to preserve BTU content amid Henry Hub pricing in the $2.50 per MMBtu range, which is below our marginal cost threshold. We've hedged 70% of our 2024 gas at $2.80, so we're prioritizing oil-weighted returns over forced gas development.

Overall, our oil cut expanded to 61% of total BOE, up from 60% in Q2 and 58% year-over-year, aligning with our strategy to high-grade our portfolio toward premium WTI-priced barrels—now trading around $82 per barrel Brent equivalent. This mix shift added about $150 million to our Q3 realized price uplift compared to a flat portfolio. Looking forward, we're guiding Q4 total production to 270,000-275,000 BOE per day, implying 2-4% sequential growth, with oil at 165,000-168,000 barrels per day. This assumes continued Permian execution, where we've secured 120 additional premium laterals through our midstream commitments with Enterprise Products. Key initiatives include piloting our first Permian waterflood pilot on 10 Wolfcamp wells, targeting 20% incremental recovery, and accelerating our Bakken stack testing with SLB's advanced fiber-optic diagnostics for real-time frac monitoring. These volumes validate our $2.2 billion 2024 capex plan—80% D&C focused—delivering a Permian FCF breakeven under $50 WTI. We've got 3.5 years of Tier 1 inventory at current pacing, and with recent M&A like our $450 million DJ Basin bolt-on, we're positioned to sustain 5-7% annual growth through the decade.

Today, I'd also like to dive deep into our lifting costs—or more precisely, our lease operating expenses, or LOE, per BOE—which remain a cornerstone of our operational efficiency. Lifting costs capture the direct cash expenses to bring a barrel of oil equivalent from the reservoir to the sales point, including pumping, compression, water handling, maintenance, and utilities, but excluding G&A, taxes, and upstream capex.

Over the past five quarters, we've seen a clear U-shaped trajectory reflective of broader industry dynamics. In Q1 2023, our company-wide LOE averaged $16.50 per BOE, benefiting from post-pandemic supply chain normalization and our early adoption of digital workflows. However, inflationary pressures—labor costs up 12% year-over-year, steel prices spiking 25% due to global supply disruptions, and power rates climbing amid natural gas volatility—pushed us to a peak of $21.20 per BOE in Q4 2023. Fast forward to Q3 2024, and we're back down to $14.80 per BOE—a 30% reduction from the peak and 10% below Q1 2023 levels. Quarter-over-quarter, that's a $1.40 or 8.5% drop.

Breaking it down regionally: Permian Basin, 65% of production, LOE fell from $12.10 per BOE in Q4 2023 to $10.20 per BOE in Q3. Eagle Ford improved from $18.50 to $15.90 per BOE. Gulf of Mexico at $28.40 per BOE down from $34.20. International steady at $22.50 per BOE.

These trends result from a multi-pronged cost reduction program launched in Q1 2024, targeting $2.00-3.00 per BOE in structural savings by year-end. Digital and AI-driven predictive maintenance using OSIsoft PI System integrations across 80% of our Permian pads has cut unplanned downtime by 25%, saving $0.45 per BOE. Chemical and fluids optimization with Nalco Champion reduced costs 22%, dodging $0.60 per BOE in disposal fees. Electrification powering 40% of pads with ERCOT grid tie-ins yielded $0.70 per BOE savings. Vendor discipline locked in 15-20% discounts, and workforce productivity via remote monitoring reduced field personnel needs by 12%.

These efforts turbocharge our full-cycle economics. At current strip prices—WTI $80s, Brent $85—we're generating $45-50 per BOE free cash flow margins. We guide Q4 LOE at $14.00-14.50 per BOE, with full-year at $15.10, aspiring to $12.50 by 2025.

Finally, on our balance sheet strength, specifically our debt levels, net debt position, and leverage ratios—a cornerstone of our financial discipline. As of September 30th, our total gross debt stood at $5.2 billion, comprising $3.8 billion in fixed-rate, investment-grade unsecured senior notes—primarily our 4.125% notes due 2028, 4.50% notes due 2031, and the recently issued 5.375% notes due 2034—and $1.4 billion drawn on our $3.0 billion syndicated revolving credit facility, which matures in 2027. Cash and equivalents totaled $1.1 billion, bringing net debt to $4.1 billion, a 22% reduction from year-end 2023. Pro forma for pending sales, net debt would be $3.5 billion.

Our trailing twelve-month EBITDAX of $2.0 billion yields a net debt to TTM EBITDAX ratio of 2.1x, down from 2.8x, well below our 1.5x-2.0x target. This deleveraging is anchored in our Tier 1 Permian core. We've repurchased $300 million in shares year-to-date, raised our dividend 10%, and expect Q4 FCF of $600 million driving leverage to 1.9x.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Rivera for an operational update.

Mike Rivera: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 265,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Catarina pad online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives, particularly in LOE as Sarah detailed.

Now I will turn it over to Jordan Lee for an update on our exploration activities.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Delaware Basin and are planning to drill 20 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Lisa Chen to discuss our marketing strategy.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Jordan. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for our NGL products in the Gulf Coast market, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact on our realizations is significant, with premiums holding firm.

I will now turn it over to Tom Patel to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Tom Patel: Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. As we wrap up our Q3 discussion, let me turn to our environmental performance around spills, incidents, and remediation efforts. At Apex Energy, our commitment to operational excellence and ESG stewardship is non-negotiable—it's core to our license to operate and path to net-zero by 2050.

In 2024 year-to-date mirroring full-year 2023 trends, we recorded zero Tier 1 spills—that's any release exceeding 1,000 barrels offshore or 5,000 barrels onshore—and just four reportable Tier 2 spills, totaling a mere 0.3 barrels of hydrocarbon volume. That's a 62% reduction in volume from prior year, well below industry benchmarks. Our total recordable incident rate improved to 0.42, lost time incident rate to 0.12, outperforming peers.

Onshore, two minor spills under 0.1 barrel from valve failures in Permian Delaware. Offshore Gulf of Mexico, one hydraulic fluid release and trace crude. Pipelines, one 0.05 barrel leak detected via ILI. Over five years, 75% reduction in spill frequency, 85% drop in volume. All spills remediated within 14 days on average, costs at $1.8 million down 45%. Techniques included ABS-approved booms achieving 99.5% recovery and bioremediation degrading 92% of residuals.

Key initiatives: 1,200 fiber-optic DAS units for AI anomaly detection, drone swarms covering 85% of acres, 24 hours training per headcount. Prevention saved $45 million last year. This de-risks our $5 billion low-carbon CCS hubs.

On ESG initiatives, particularly emissions reduction: Fiscal year-to-date, against 2019 baseline of 45 million metric tons CO2e, we've achieved 28% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 to 32.4 million metric tons. Methane intensity to 0.23%, flaring at 0.8%. Scope 3 down 15% to 180 million metric tons.

Methane abatement via OGI cameras on 85% of wells, capturing 450 tons methane Q4 equivalent. CCUS Apex Hub at 2.5 million metric tons per annum, Phase 2 FID Q2 2025. Electrified 65% Gulf of Mexico fleet. Permian halved intensity to 8 kg CO2e per BOE. Allocating 12% capex to low-carbon.

We'll hit 35% cuts by 2025. This is alpha generation, with 75% ESG-labeled financing.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Ramirez with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on production guidance for next quarter and full year, including factors influencing projections?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thanks, John. Great question on production guidance—it's core to our value creation story here at Apex Energy. For Q4, we're guiding to 270,000 to 275,000 BOE per day, implying about 3% sequential growth from Q3's realized 265,000 BOE per day. Oil volumes will make up roughly 62% of that mix. For full year 2024, we now expect 600,000 to 620,000 BOE per day at midpoint, up 12% above 2023.

The growth catalysts: Our D&C program bringing online 45 to 50 new wells, primarily Delaware Basin pads with ApexMax design, initial 30-day IPs of 1,800 BOE per day per well, up 15% via proppant intensity. Permian 78% of production, accelerating post-acquisition of 15,000 net acres. Eagle Ford refracs, GoM tie-backs.

Offsetting declines of 25,000 BOE per day quarterly with 35 to 40 workovers. Headwinds like frac constraints mitigated by Patterson-UTI access. Macro supportive with WTI $78-82. Risks like hurricanes baked in, ESG embedded with methane under 0.2%. Full-year capex $1.8-1.9 billion yielding $1.2 billion FCF.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Good morning. What are your expectations for environmental performance going forward?

Tom Patel: Good morning, David. On environmental performance, we're on track for sub-0.2 TRIR in 2025, targeting zero spill volumes. Our tech like DAS and drones, plus training, positions us ahead of peers amid SEC rules.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Could you please provide more color on ESG initiatives?

Tom Patel: Thanks, Emily. As detailed, 28% Scope 1/2 reduction, methane 0.23%, flaring near zero. CCUS ramping to 5 million metric tons per annum, electrification key. Targeting 35% cuts by 2025, with IRR >15% on low-carbon capex.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kim with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Robert Kim: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Jordan Lee: Robert, our Delaware seismic and 20 wells will add reserves, high-grading inventory with breakevens under $45 WTI. This sustains 5-7% CAGR, integrating with midstream for 50%+ IRR.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sophia Grant with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sophia Grant: What is the outlook for the new product in the coming years?

Lisa Chen: Sophia, strong demand for NGLs in Gulf Coast, with propane exports up 25%. We'll expand via Mont Belvieu, strengthening realizations amid Asia demand.

Operator: Our next question comes from Michael Torres with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Michael Torres: Could you elaborate on your debt strategy?

Sarah Jenkins: Michael, net debt to 1.9x by year-end, liquidity $2.5 billion. Focus on deleveraging via FCF, M&A optionality in Permian.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
